root_cause.text: In the BPF JIT constant-blinding clone/replace path, `bpf_jit_prog_release_other()` updated `aux->prog` but not the dev-bound XDP offload back-pointer `aux->offload->prog`, leaving `offload->prog` dangling to a freed original `bpf_prog`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (fp->aux->offload) fp->aux->offload->prog = fp;` immediately after `fp->aux->prog = fp;`, and the CVE/commit message explicitly states that constant blinding clones the program, frees the original, and later `bpf_dev_bound_netdev_unregister()` calls `__bpf_prog_offload_destroy(offload->prog)` on the stale freed pointer, causing the page fault.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update the offload program reference when releasing the alternate BPF program instance so offload state points to the surviving program.
intent_record.what: In `bpf_jit_prog_release_other`, after assigning `fp->aux->prog = fp;`, the change adds a conditional check for `fp->aux->offload` and, when present, assigns `fp->aux->offload->prog = fp` before calling `bpf_prog_clone_free(fp_other)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this keeps the offload-associated program pointer synchronized with the surviving `fp` object when releasing the other program instance, preventing the offload state from continuing to reference the wrong or freed program structure.

grouping_result.intent: Update the offload program reference when releasing the alternate BPF program instance so offload state points to the surviving program.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the root cause by updating the XDP offload back-pointer (`aux->offload->prog`) when replacing/releasing the alternate BPF program, preventing it from dangling to the freed original `bpf_prog`.

candidates.rationale: This updates only aux->prog to the surviving program during the clone/original replacement path, but fails to also update aux->offload->prog, causing the offload back-pointer to remain pointed at the soon-to-be-freed alternate program.
This frees the alternate program instance while the offload back-pointer was not redirected, making aux->offload->prog dangle to freed memory.

vuln_statements.explanation: This replacement path updates only the generic aux->prog pointer to the surviving program, but omits updating the XDP offload back-pointer aux->offload->prog. That omission is the root cause that leaves offload state still referencing the other program instance.
After aux->prog is updated without also redirecting aux->offload->prog, freeing fp_other causes the stale offload->prog back-pointer to become dangling and reference freed memory.
